NASB.1: Ephraim feeds on wind, And pursues the east wind continually; He multiplies lies and violence. Moreover, he makes a covenant with Assyria, And oil is carried to Egypt.
NASB.2: The LORD also has a dispute with Judah, And will punish Jacob according to his ways; He will repay him according to his deeds.
NASB.3: In the womb he took his brother by the heel, And in his maturity he contended with God.
NASB.4: Yes, he wrestled with the angel and prevailed; He wept and sought His favor. He found Him at Bethel And there He spoke with us,
NASB.5: Even the LORD, the God of hosts, The LORD is His name.
NASB.6: Therefore, return to your God, Observe kindness and justice, And wait for your God continually.
NASB.7: A merchant, in whose hands are false balances, He loves to oppress.
NASB.8: And Ephraim said, 'Surely I have become rich, I have found wealth for myself; In all my labors they will find in me No iniquity, which [would be] sin.'
NASB.9: But I [have been] the LORD your God since the land of Egypt; I will make you live in tents again, As in the days of the appointed festival.
NASB.10: I have also spoken to the prophets, And I gave numerous visions, And through the prophets I gave parables.
NASB.11: Is there iniquity [in] Gilead? Surely they are worthless. In Gilgal they sacrifice bulls, Yes, their altars are like the stone heaps Beside the furrows of the field.
NASB.12: Now Jacob fled to the land of Aram, And Israel worked for a wife, And for a wife he kept [sheep].
NASB.13: But by a prophet the LORD brought Israel from Egypt, And by a prophet he was kept.
NASB.14: Ephraim has provoked to bitter anger; So his Lord will leave his bloodguilt on him And bring back his reproach to him.

NKJV.1: “Ephraim feeds on the wind, And pursues the east wind; He daily increases lies and desolation.  Also they make a covenant with the Assyrians, And oil is carried to Egypt.
NKJV.2: “The LORD also brings a charge against Judah, And will punish Jacob according to his ways; According to his deeds He will recompense him.
NKJV.3: He took his brother by the heel in the womb, And in his strength he struggled with God.
NKJV.4: Yes, he struggled with the Angel and prevailed; He wept, and sought favor from Him. He found Him in Bethel, And there He spoke to us—
NKJV.5: That is, the LORD God of hosts. The LORD is His memorable name.
NKJV.6: So you, by the help of your God, return; Observe mercy and justice, And wait on your God continually.
NKJV.7: “A cunning Canaanite! Deceitful scales are in his hand; He loves to oppress.
NKJV.8: And Ephraim said, ‘Surely I have become rich, I have found wealth for myself; In all my labors They shall find in me no iniquity that is sin.’
NKJV.9: “But I am the LORD your God, Ever since the land of Egypt; I will again make you dwell in tents, As in the days of the appointed feast.
NKJV.10: I have also spoken by the prophets, And have multiplied visions; I have given symbols through the witness of the prophets.”
NKJV.11: Though Gilead has idols— Surely they are vanity— Though they sacrifice bulls in Gilgal, Indeed their altars shall be heaps in the furrows of the field.
NKJV.12: Jacob fled to the country of Syria; Israel served for a spouse, And for a wife he tended sheep.
NKJV.13: By a prophet the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt, And by a prophet he was preserved.
NKJV.14: Ephraim provoked Him to anger most bitterly; Therefore his Lord will leave the guilt of his bloodshed upon him, And return his reproach upon him.

ESV.1: Ephraim feeds on the wind and pursues the east wind all day long; they multiply falsehood and violence; they make a covenant with Assyria, and oil is carried to Egypt.
ESV.2: The LORD has an indictment against Judah and will punish Jacob according to his ways; he will repay him according to his deeds.
ESV.3: In the womb he took his brother by the heel, and in his manhood he strove with God.
ESV.4: He strove with the angel and prevailed; he wept and sought his favor. He met God  at Bethel, and there God spoke with us —
ESV.5: the LORD, the God of hosts, the LORD is his memorial name:
ESV.6: “So you, by the help of your God, return, hold fast to love and justice, and wait continually for your God.”
ESV.7: A merchant, in whose hands are false balances, he loves to oppress.
ESV.8: Ephraim has said, “Ah, but I am rich; I have found wealth for myself; in all my labors they cannot find in me iniquity or sin.”
ESV.9: I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt; I will again make you dwell in tents, as in the days of the appointed feast.
ESV.10: I spoke to the prophets; it was I who multiplied visions, and through the prophets gave parables.
ESV.11: If there is iniquity in Gilead, they shall surely come to nothing: in Gilgal they sacrifice bulls; their altars also are like stone heaps on the furrows of the field.
ESV.12: Jacob fled to the land of Aram; there Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he guarded sheep.
ESV.13: By a prophet the LORD brought Israel up from Egypt, and by a prophet he was guarded.
ESV.14: Ephraim has given bitter provocation; so his Lord will leave his bloodguilt on him and will repay him for his disgraceful deeds.

NLT.1:
The people of Israel feed on the wind;
they chase after the east wind all day long.
They pile up lies and violence;
they are making an alliance with Assyria
while sending olive oil to buy support from Egypt.
NLT.2:
Now the LORD is bringing charges against Judah.
He is about to punish Jacob for all his deceitful ways,
and pay him back for all he has done.
NLT.3:
Even in the womb,
Jacob struggled with his brother;
when he became a man,
he even fought with God.
NLT.4:
Yes, he wrestled with the angel and won.
He wept and pleaded for a blessing from him.
There at Bethel he met God face to face,
and God spoke to him —
NLT.5:
the LORD God of Heaven’s Armies,
the LORD is his name!
NLT.6:
So now, come back to your God.
Act with love and justice,
and always depend on him.
NLT.7:
But no, the people are like crafty merchants
selling from dishonest scales —
they love to cheat.
NLT.8:
Israel boasts, “I am rich!
I’ve made a fortune all by myself!
No one has caught me cheating!
My record is spotless!”
NLT.9:
“But I am the LORD your God,
who rescued you from slavery in Egypt.
And I will make you live in tents again,
as you do each year at the Festival of Shelters.
NLT.10:
I sent my prophets to warn you
with many visions and parables.”
NLT.11:
But the people of Gilead are worthless
because of their idol worship.
And in Gilgal, too, they sacrifice bulls;
their altars are lined up like the heaps of stone
along the edges of a plowed field.
NLT.12:
Jacob fled to the land of Aram,
and there he earned a wife by tending sheep.
NLT.13:
Then by a prophet
the LORD brought Jacob’s descendants out of Egypt;
and by that prophet
they were protected.
NLT.14:
But the people of Israel
have bitterly provoked the LORD,
so their Lord will now sentence them to death
in payment for their sins.

AMP.1:
Ephraim feeds on the [emptiness of the] wind
And [continually] pursues the [parching] east wind [which brings destruction];
Every day he multiplies lies and violence.
Further, he makes a covenant with Assyria
And (olive) oil is carried to Egypt [to seek alliances].
AMP.2:
The LORD also has a dispute [a legal complaint and an indictment] with Judah,
And He will punish Jacob in accordance with his ways;
He will repay him in accordance with his deeds.
AMP.3:
In their mother's womb he took his brother by the heel,
And in his maturity he contended with God.
AMP.4:
He wrestled with the angel and prevailed;
He wept [in repentance] and sought His favor.
He met Him at Bethel
And there God spoke with [him and through him with] us—
AMP.5:
Even the LORD, the God of hosts,
The name of Him [who spoke with Jacob] is the LORD.
AMP.6:
Therefore, return [in repentance] to your God,
Observe and highly regard kindness and justice,
And wait [expectantly] for your God continually.
AMP.7:
A merchant, in whose hand are false and fraudulent balances;
He loves to oppress and exploit.
AMP.8:
Ephraim said, "I have indeed become rich [and powerful as a nation];
I have found wealth for myself.
In all my labors they will not find in me
Any wickedness that would be sin."
AMP.9:
But I have been the LORD your God since [you became a nation in] the land of Egypt;
I will make you live in tents again,
As in the days of the appointed and solemn festival.
AMP.10:
I have also spoken to [you through] the prophets,
And I gave [them] many visions [to make My will known],
And through the prophets I gave parables [to appeal to your sense of right and wrong].
AMP.11:
Is there wickedness (idolatry) in Gilead?
Surely the people there are worthless.
In Gilgal [they defy Me when] they sacrifice bulls,
Yes, [after My judgment] their [pagan] altars are like the stone heaps
In the furrows of the fields.
AMP.12:
Now Jacob (Israel) fled into the open country of Aram (Paddan-aram),
And [there] Israel (Jacob) worked and served for a wife,
And for a wife he kept sheep.
AMP.13:
And by a prophet (Moses) the LORD brought Israel up from Egypt,
And by a prophet Israel was preserved.
AMP.14:
Ephraim has provoked most bitter anger;
So his Lord will leave his bloodguilt on him [invoking punishment]
And bring back to him his shame and dishonor.

MSG.1:
Ephraim, obsessed with god-fantasies,
chases ghosts and phantoms.
He tells lies nonstop,
soul-destroying lies.
Both Ephraim and Judah made deals with Assyria
and tried to get an inside track with Egypt.
MSG.2:
God is bringing charges against Israel.
Jacob's children are hauled into court to be punished.
MSG.3:
In the womb, that heel, Jacob, got the best of his brother.
When he grew up, he tried to get the best of God.
MSG.4:
But God would not be bested.
God bested him.
Brought to his knees,
Jacob wept and prayed.
God found him at Bethel.
That's where he spoke with him.
MSG.6:
What are you waiting for? Return to your God!
Commit yourself in love, in justice!
Wait for your God,
and don't give up on him—ever!
MSG.7:
The businessmen engage in wholesale fraud.
They love to rip people off!
MSG.8:
Ephraim boasted, "Look, I'm rich!
I've made it big!
And look how well I've covered my tracks:
not a hint of fraud, not a sign of sin!"
MSG.9:
"But not so fast! I'm God, your God!
Your God from the days in Egypt!
I'm going to put you back to living in tents,
as in the old days when you worshiped in the wilderness.
MSG.10:
I speak through the prophets
to give clear pictures of the way things are.
Using prophets, I tell revealing stories.
MSG.11:
I show Gilead rampant with religious scandal
and Gilgal teeming with empty-headed religion.
I expose their worship centers as
stinking piles of garbage in their gardens."
MSG.12:
Are you going to repeat the life of your ancestor Jacob?
He ran off guilty to Aram,
Then sold his soul to get ahead,
and made it big through treachery and deceit.
MSG.13:
Your real identity is formed through God-sent prophets,
who led you out of Egypt and served as faithful pastors.
MSG.14:
As it is, Ephraim has continually
and inexcusably insulted God.
Now he has to pay for his life-destroying ways.
His Master will do to him what he has done.

NET.1: Ephraim continually feeds on the wind; he chases the east wind all day; he multiplies lies and violence. They make treaties with Assyria, and send olive oil as tribute to Egypt.
NET.2: The LORD also has a covenant lawsuit against Judah; he will punish Jacob according to his ways and repay him according to his deeds.
NET.3: In the womb he attacked his brother; in his manly vigor he struggled with God.
NET.4: He struggled with an angel and prevailed; he wept and begged for his favor. He found God at Bethel, and there he spoke with him!
NET.5: As for the LORD God Almighty, the LORD is the name by which he is remembered!
NET.6: But you must return to your God, by maintaining love and justice, and by waiting for your God to return to you.
NET.7: The businessmen love to cheat; they use dishonest scales.
NET.8: Ephraim boasts, “I am very rich! I have become wealthy! In all that I have done to gain my wealth, no one can accuse me of any offense that is actually sinful.”
NET.9: “I am the LORD your God who brought you out of Egypt; I will make you live in tents again as in the days of old.
NET.10: I spoke to the prophets; I myself revealed many visions; I spoke in parables through the prophets.”
NET.11: Is there idolatry in Gilead? Certainly its inhabitants will come to nothing! Do they sacrifice bulls in Gilgal? Surely their altars will be like stones heaped up on a plowed field!
NET.12: Jacob fled to the country of Aram, then Israel worked to acquire a wife; he tended sheep to pay for her.
NET.13: The LORD brought Israel out of Egypt by a prophet, and due to a prophet Israel was preserved alive.
NET.14: But Ephraim bitterly provoked him to anger; so he will hold him accountable for the blood he has shed, his Lord will repay him for the contempt he has shown.
